ideas.title: Knock the pears down with the boomerang
same_form: Skipping stones, a take that misses
ideas.critique: It is the boomerang again, and a film of three throws looks a lot like the last post. What is new is real: ray-cast collisions against the island's own triangles and pears that fall and roll make it a skill toy instead of a flight study, but the film only stands apart if the clack and the drop are clearly readable.

ideas.title: A hot-air balloon that rides the wind layers
ideas.critique: The island has never had a vehicle you steer only through physics, and reading a wind that turns with height is a puzzle with a clear win. The layered wind is a scripted field, so the realism rests on the heat and buoyancy model, and a slow drift can make a dull film unless the turn over the sea is caught.

ideas.title: A trebuchet built from planks
ideas.nearest: Skipping stones, a take that misses
same_form: Skipping stones, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Jointed rigid bodies, a verlet sling and a fracturing pumpkin would be new mechanisms, and aiming at a target ring is a loop people replay. But it is the third launched-projectile film in a row of thrown things, and a trebuchet is the first siege toy anyone would predict.

ideas.title: A snowball that grows as you roll it
ideas.critique: A GPU snow field that the ball eats into, leaving a track while its mass grows, is a real two-way coupling the island has never had, and a ball that runs away downhill is good to watch. Stacking a snowman is the most expected payoff, and the stacking is where it will probably fall back on scripting.

ideas.title: A sandcastle against the tide
ideas.critique: The island already has slumping sand heightfields; what is new is the wetness field that changes the angle of repose, plus waves that carry sand away. That is a real granular step, but on a heightfield sandcastle walls look like soft bumps, and digging with a cursor risks feeling like a paint tool.

ideas.title: A raft of driftwood logs
ideas.critique: Buoyancy from the submerged volume of several sprung bodies is new and something to build on, and a capsize is a funny film. It shares the 'reach the islet' goal with the balloon, and dragging and lashing logs can turn into chores before the fun part.

ideas.title: A marble run down the hill
ideas.critique: Glass marbles under a path tracer really do show off light, and building a course is the kind of sandbox people come back to. A builder mode where you lay track is a familiar genre, and rolling contact against meshes is fragile, so marbles clipping through chutes would ruin the film.

ideas.title: Spinning tops on the pier
ideas.critique: Proper gyroscopic precession and nutation, and a top lying down in a slow spiral, is physics you cannot fake convincingly, so it would read as real. The duel is thin as a game: pull the string and watch, with little control after the throw.

ideas.title: Paper planes from the lookout
same_form: Skipping stones, a take that misses
ideas.critique: This is the paper-page flight code once more, thrown instead of dropped, right after the boomerang, and the film of three throws is the same shape as that post. Folding the trim is a real control and a farthest-glide marker gives a reason to come back, but nobody who knows the island will be surprised.

ideas.title: Sneak past the owl
ideas.critique: It turns the owl and the echo work into something you can play, and making footstep loudness depend on the ground material is a real use of the acoustics. A stealth crossing is the obvious game for a listening owl, and a night film of a small friend creeping risks being as dark and still as the earlier night takes.
